subject: DPA discussion: backup/DR carve-out, retention windows, and subprocessor approvals
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cobaltmedical.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Cobalt IT <it@cobaltmedical.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: DPA draft questions — retention & DR carve-out

Hi Sean / Monica,

Thanks again for the redlined DPA (v3). We did a line-by-line with our legal and infosec teams and have a few open items before we can proceed to execution via DocuSign:

1) Retention window: Section 4.2 currently reads "retain customer content for up to 7 years" — our policy requires a configurable default of 1 year with the ability to extend per-account. Can you confirm Redwood can support a 12-month default on our tenant?

2) Backup/DR carve-out: Our auditors want an explicit carve-out that allows emergency restores for incident response, but limited to a defined process and logging. The current DR language is very broad. Can Redwood provide proposed guardrails (who can request, audit trail, retention of restore logs)?

3) Subprocessors: Please confirm the latest subprocessor roster. We received an internal list (attached) that doesn't match the DPA appendix. If AWS or GCP are considered subprocessors for storage/compute, we need confirmation of region restrictions (no egress to eu-west for our datasets).

I've attached our redlines and a cleaned CSV of our current subprocessor concerns. If helpful, our counsel Samir Khan can join a short call this week to close these items.

Next steps: Ideally we get confirmation on the three bullets above and then we can sign. Please advise if you want to accept our redlines, propose alternative wording, or set up a review call.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Cobalt Medical

Attachments: Cobalt_DPA_v3_redlines.docx, subprocessors_list_20261129.csv

From: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cobaltmedical.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA draft questions — retention & DR carve-out

Elena — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Quick responses inline below; collecting a couple items from engineering to give concrete language for the DR guardrails.

1) Retention window: Yes — Redwood supports a per-customer retention config. Default for hosted tenants is 12 months; we can include a sentence in Section 4.2 that states "default retention for Customer Content is 12 months, configurable by mutual agreement." If Cobalt prefers an explicit 12-month cap in the DPA we can accept that.

2) Backup/DR carve-out: We agree that the DPA should limit emergency restores to authorized personnel and require an auditable request flow. Monica, can you draft the suggested wording (who may request, ticketing/audit, TTL for restore snapshots)?

3) Subprocessors: Our canonical list is in the current DPA appendix. I'll attach the latest export from our vendor registry; it includes AWS (us-west-2) as storage/compute and GCP for analytics (only us-east1). We can add a clause restricting egress locations for Cobalt's data if required — let's confirm the specific regions you need to block.

I can sync with Samir on a 30-min call if that helps move to DocuSign. Proposed times: Thu 12/3 9am PT or Fri 12/4 11am PT.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com)

Attachments: redlines_compare.pdf

From: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cobaltmedical.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 08:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA draft questions — retention & DR carve-out

Elena — following up with the proposed DR wording below (we can bake into Section 7.3):

"Backup and Emergency Restore. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may, in accordance with its documented incident response procedures and upon authorization by Customer's designated security contact, access backup snapshots to perform emergency restores solely to remediate Security Incidents affecting the Customer. All such accesses will be logged, retained for a minimum of 24 months, and subject to audit by Customer on reasonable notice. Redwood will maintain a ticket reference for each restore request and will provide a post‑incident restore report within 10 business days."

Key notes:
- Authorized requestors: security lead or designated technical contact listed in the SOW; requests must be made through our ticketing system (link below).
- Snapshot TTL: restored artifacts are retained for up to 30 days post-restore unless Customer requests longer retention.

If that aligns, we can incorporate into the DPA and send updated v4 for your review. Happy to jump on the call with Samir.

Monica Patel
Dir, Product Security Ops
Redwood Inference

Related link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2191

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cobaltmedical.com>
To: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@cobaltmedical.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 10:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA draft questions — retention & DR carve-out

Monica — thanks, that language looks much better. A few small asks from counsel:

• Please change "retain for a minimum of 24 months" (logs) to 36 months, per our audit requirements.
• Can you add that the ticket system will capture requester identity and the justification for restore? We don't need the full ticket content but want proof of approval and scope.
• On Snapshot TTL — Cobalt requests a 90-day retention for restored artifacts where the restore is performed as part of an investigation. We accept 30 days for routine business restores.

Samir is available on Mon 12/7 8:30am PT for a 30-min call to finalize. After we agree to these points, we can route to our procurement team for signature.

Best,
Elena

Subject: Re: DPA draft questions — retention & DR carve-out

Elena / Samir — great to meet on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposal so procurement can move to DocuSign: 

1) Logs retention: Redwood will retain restore/audit logs for 36 months and include requester identity and justification in the ticket metadata.
2) Snapshot TTL: Redwood will implement a tiered TTL: 30 days for standard restores; 90 days for investigatory restores (must be flagged in the ticket with justification).
3) Regional restrictions: We will add an appendix: "Customer-specified geographic restrictions" listing permitted regions for Cobalt data (us-west-2, us-east-1). We will not egress Cobalt production data to eu-west unless mutually agreed in writing.

Action items: Sean to send updated DPA v4 (redlined) and route to DocuSign envelope. Monica will add the DR text to 7.3; Legal ops will attach the subprocessor CSV that defines region locations.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Cobalt_DPA_v4_redlines.docx (to follow in envelope)

- Subprocessor appendix updated to reflect storage/compute locations (attached CSV)

Next steps: Elena/Samir — please review the envelope and sign. If procurement needs the one-page SOW addendum, we'll attach it to the envelope as a separate document.

If you want, I can request a final one-day extension to attach the SOW, otherwise please sign and we'll treat the SOW as a follow-up appendix.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.
